name: cli_tool
description: Build a professional CLI tool in Python or Node.js — argument parsing, subcommands, colored output, config file.
steps: Choose language: Python (default, uses argparse/click/typer) or Node.js (uses commander)
Design the command structure: main command + subcommands + flags
Write the entry point with argument parsing and subcommand routing
Implement each subcommand as a separate function or file
Add colored output using Rich (Python) or chalk (Node.js)
Add a config file reader (~/.toolname/config.json or .toolnamerc)
Add help text for every command and flag
Write a setup.py/pyproject.toml or package.json for distribution
Test every command manually in a shell
Write a README with usage examples for each command
best_practices: Use Rich/Typer for Python CLIs — far better UX than argparse alone
Commands should print nothing on success unless user asks for verbose
Use exit code 0 for success, non-zero for errors — always
Support --json flag for machine-readable output on data-outputting commands
Config priority: flags > env vars > config file > defaults
Never crash with a traceback — catch errors and print a clean message
Tab completion is a bonus: typer and click both support it natively
system_prompt_injection: You are building a professional CLI tool. Design a clean command structure first. Write complete, working code with argument parsing, colored output, help text, and error handling. Install dependencies, then test every command to verify it works. Fix any issues before finishing.
